verdict.line: You lose if you let Nasus farm Siphoning Strike stacks uncontested past level 6; you win if you force stuns through Facebreaker before his Fury of the Sands comes online.

brief.thesis: Nasus is a scaling threat whose power is entirely gated by Q (Siphoning Strike) last-hits, not levels or items — every stack he gets is permanent and uncontested lane equals a lost lane. Sett has no way to interrupt the Q animation, so the only lever is denying him CS volume early through all-in pressure, which matches the 46.3% head-to-head over 123 games despite Sett holding the lane-advantage tag.

theirWindow.what: Every uncontested Siphoning Strike is permanent bonus damage he keeps for the whole game. If you let him free-farm CS from level 1-6 you've already lost the lane regardless of your own damage.

yourWindow.when: he's on cooldown or out of position
yourWindow.what: Siphoning Strike is 8/7/6/5/4s cooldown — after he throws it on a minion, punish the window with E (Facebreaker) to pull him and a minion together for the stun, then Q (Knuckle Down) auto-reset damage. He has no dash, so a good Facebreaker angle is a free combo every time.

start.why: Picked in 86.4% of games at a 42.8% win rate over 152 games — the lifesteal and AD sustain let you keep all-inning through his Soul Eater lifesteal in the trades that actually matter before level 6.

boots.why: 50% win rate over 68 games and the higher pick rate (41.5%) — the flat physical damage reduction directly counters his Q poke and auto-reset damage while you're forcing stun windows.

core.why: Core first item in both top build paths (31% and 7.1% pick share) — the slow-on-hit lets you stick to him through Wither's own slow and land full Facebreaker combos.
Appears in the top two build paths at 53.8% and 33.3% win rate — the armor shred compounds with your burst windows before his Fury of the Sands health pool makes him unkillable.
Top-performing third item at 53.8% win rate over 26 games — bonus health and damage-over-time scale your trades as his stacks make him tankier.

you're ahead and want to out-sustain his lifesteal in extended all-ins rather than trade burst

runes.keystoneWhy: Conqueror's stacking adaptive damage and healing rewards exactly the extended-trade, stick-on-him playstyle Sett needs to punish Nasus before his stacks snowball — matches both top rune pages (45.6% and 56.5% pick share).

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 86.6% of games at 44.3% win rate — Ignite's burn closes the kill window during your early all-ins before his Soul Eater lifesteal can pull him back out of kill range.

playing.title: Punish every Q animation
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike has an 8-to-4s cooldown and no dash attached — the instant he commits to it on a minion, step in with E (Facebreaker) to pull him alongside the minion for the stun.

playing.title: All-in before level 6 ends
playing.detail: His stacks are worthless if he's dead or shoved off minions. Use Q (Knuckle Down)'s empowered attacks plus W (Haymaker)'s stored Grit shield to win short trades repeatedly from level 1-5.

playing.title: Track his Wither cooldown
playing.detail: W (Wither) is 15-to-11s cooldown and decelerates your Move Speed and Attack Speed — don't commit to a long stick-fight the moment he lands it, since your Stridebreaker slow and Facebreaker range are what keep you in range, not raw speed.

playing.title: Save R for an isolated punish
playing.detail: The Show Stopper carries him alone through the air and slams him, slowing anyone near the landing spot — use it when he's overextended past minions, not as a poke tool, since its 120s base cooldown means a wasted cast gives him a full stack-farming window.

playing.title: Respect Spirit Fire zone control
playing.detail: E (Spirit Fire) is a 12s-cooldown ground zone that reduces armor while you stand in it — don't facecheck or stand in an unclaimed Spirit Fire patch during trades, it directly amplifies his Q damage on you.

playing.title: Ward for his Fury of the Sands timer
playing.detail: Once he hits 6 with Fury of the Sands up, his range and health balloon for its duration — avoid extended 1v1s during an active ult past level 11-15 and instead bait him to use it early, then punish the 120s cooldown gap.

playing.title: Close the lane before 15 minutes
playing.detail: Every uncontested wave is permanent Q stacks for him — track CS parity on the minimap, not just your own farm, since this matchup's 46.3% win rate over 123 games reflects games where Sett let him scale unchecked.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and trade-window calls are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Nasus grow during early game by applying pressure and gaining lane control. Use your abilities whenever the come off cooldown to deal damage.
